cells.tense: The practice is running now, and it runs without being forced.
cells.act: let one structure collapse that could not hold
cells.ask: Take the habit in your practice that's already failing, set it down, and spend the week without rebuilding it. Notice the floor it leaves.
cells.core:
The practice is going well, and the good part is that you're not dragging it. Sessions add up, and the skill gets finer instead of tighter. Time by yourself connects you to people rather than separating you from them, and you can name whether a session counted on the day it happened.
There's something you're propping up out of habit, though — a rule about how the work has to go, an arrangement that stopped earning its place. Let it come down. Stop holding it up and see whether anything leans on it. What was carrying weight stays where it is; what drops was only taking up the floor you need.

cells.tense: The practice is being run toward a version of it that has not arrived yet.
cells.act: release it on purpose, not by losing it
cells.ask: Before the next session, decide out loud one thing that counts as finished, and stop there when you reach it.
cells.core:
You're sharpening something that mostly works, and from inside that reads as care. The unfinished next version pulls harder than what's under your hands, and quitting for the day doesn't feel like a choice you have. The sessions keep you alone more than they used to, and that alone time has stopped feeling chosen.
What's asked is smaller than it sounds. Before you start the next session, say out loud what finished will look like, then stop exactly there. Nothing falls apart when you do. You find out the practice isn't holding you up by the throat, and the next session comes easier because you know you can set it down.

cells.tense: The practice stalled some time back, and the open ground has not been safe to stand on since.
cells.act: let an exchange flow both ways
cells.ask: Ask one person one real question about something you want to learn, let the answer land, and hand back something you know. Then stop.
cells.core:
There's a door behind you that you don't walk through anymore, and this kind of work sits on the far side of it. The sessions you keep are small enough not to count. Nothing you do gets deeper. You show up for other people; you don't show up to be shown anything.
Something gets honed only in an exchange — someone shows you a thing, you hand back what you found. Try one turn of that this week. A real question asked of one person, their answer let in, and something you know handed back. One turn each way is the whole trade. The door is where it was.

cells.tense: The practice is already underway, and you would not name it that.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: Write a short note of what you can do now that you couldn't before, in your own hand, and put it where you'll find it later.
cells.core:
You know things you didn't set out to learn. Your hands move well in territory you couldn't draw. Ask how you got good and the story is that it just happened, or that it's nobody's business. There are real hours behind what you can do, and the name isn't on it.
One small true sentence, in your own hand — what you can do now that you couldn't before — left somewhere you'll find it later. No plan on top of it, nothing to build. A thing said plainly is easier to draw on later than a thing you've been carrying unnamed.
